# Connect the hub to the sandbox runtime and define profiles

## Intent

Sandboxes are optional in Parley and run on OpenShell, not in the hub. This package is what turns the feature on safely: an operator points the hub at one OpenShell gateway and declares the sandbox profiles agents may use, the hub refuses to start on a configuration or a gateway it cannot work with, and from then on every sandbox route is decided by one set of rules about who may read, who may write and who may act through a sandbox. It also gives the rest of the sandbox work one client to the runtime, so that no other part of the hub talks to OpenShell on its own.

## Goals

- A hub without a `[sandbox]` section contacts no runtime, and every sandbox route answers HTTP 404 with `error_type` `sandboxes_disabled` to an authenticated caller.
- A `[sandbox]` section with several mistakes stops the start with exit status 1 and one error line that names every offending key; no message contains a credential.
- With a valid section the hub contacts the gateway once at start, within 30 seconds: it authenticates, checks the release, makes sure its OpenShell workspace exists, installs the provider profile of the hub credential, checks every configured provider profile and validates every profile's policy file. Any failure stops the start with a message that names the key or the profile.
- After a successful start, losing the gateway never stops the hub: the runtime client reports the runtime as unreachable, routes that need it answer HTTP 502 with `error_type` `sandbox_runtime_error`, and routes that read stored state keep answering.
- `GET /sandbox-profiles` lists the profiles in name order without policy paths, `env` values or secret values; `parley sandbox profiles` prints that list.
- `GET /sandboxes` lists the sandboxes of every workspace, newest first, to the admin token only.
- Packages 45 to 48 get: the loaded configuration and profiles; one runtime client interface with an OpenShell implementation and an in-memory fake that pass the same contract tests; route declarations that apply the sandbox check order, scopes and workspace needs; and the no-widening decision.

That package also supplies the sandbox source that `GET /sandboxes` of this package reads.

- Stop, start, idle stop, expiry, delete, checkpoints, reconciliation on `reconcile_interval`, record cleanup and the behaviour at hub shutdown: package 47 sandbox_lifecycle_and_checkpoints.
- The effective policy, denials, proposals, approve and reject, workspace sandbox rules, the use of `allow_workspace_rules` and the workspace-scope authority of SBX-FR-070: package 48 sandbox_network_policy. The refusal of workspace-bound tokens on approve and reject (`403 token_bound`, SBX-FR-014) is declared by that package with the declaration of package 08 workspace_bound_tokens, which is not a dependency of this one.
- The scope registry that holds `sandboxes:read` and `sandboxes:write` whether or not sandboxes are enabled (SBX-FR-004), the scope check and the glob cover rule: package 06 api_keys_and_access_tokens. This package calls them.
- The binding guard and its allowlist, on which `GET /sandbox-profiles` stands: package 08 workspace_bound_tokens.
- The metric catalogue, the registry and `/metrics`: package 51 audit_query_and_retention. This package declares the recorder interface the sandbox packages report through and reports `parley_sandbox_runtime_up`; the other sandbox metrics are reported by packages 45 to 48.

## Requirements

### Feature switch (SBX-FR-001, SBX-FR-004)

Sandboxes are on when the configuration file has a `[sandbox]` section, also an empty one (which is then invalid, because `gateway_url` is required). Without the section the hub builds no runtime client, contacts no gateway, runs no sandbox background work, and leaves stored sandbox records as they are. `GET /version` then has no `sandbox_runtime` member. The scopes `sandboxes:read` and `sandboxes:write` exist either way (package 06).

### Static validation of `[sandbox]` (SBX-FR-002, §13.9)

Validation runs when the configuration is loaded, before any data is opened. It checks everything below, collects every failure and reports them together as one error. Each failure names its key: `sandbox.<key>`, `sandbox.profiles[<name>].<key>` or `sandbox.credentials[<name>].<key>` (the zero-based index in place of the name when the entry has no usable name). The process exits with status 1 and one error line on stderr, as for every configuration error (package 03). An unknown key in `[sandbox]`, in a profile or in a credential entry is a failure like the others. No message contains the content of `token_file` or `oidc_client_secret_file`, and a `gateway_url` or `oidc_issuer` is never echoed with user information.

| Key | Type | Default | Valid |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runtime` | string | `openshell` | `openshell` only |
| `gateway_url` | URL | required | `https://host[:port]`; `http` only when the host is `localhost`, an address in `127.0.0.0/8` or `::1`; no user information, no query, no fragment, and no path other than `/` |
| `tls_cert`, `tls_key` | path | `""` | both or neither; each a readable file |
| `tls_ca` | path | `""` | a readable file |
| `token_file` | path | `""` | a readable file whose content, without surrounding white space, is not empty |
| `oidc_issuer`, `oidc_client_id`, `oidc_client_secret_file` | URL, string, path | `""` | all three or none; the issuer by the URL rule of `gateway_url`; the secret file readable and not empty |
| `openshell_workspace` | string | `parley` | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$` |
| `max_ttl` | duration | `24h` | more than 0 |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `30m` | 0 or more; 0 disables |
| `max_sandboxes` | int | `200` | at least 1 |
| `max_per_org` | int | `100` | at least 1 and at most `max_sandboxes` |
| `max_per_workspace` | int | `50` | at least 1 |
| `max_per_user` | int | `20` | at least 1 |
| `allow_workspace_rules` | bool | `true` | |
| `max_exec_timeout` | duration | `30m` | more than 0 |
| `max_concurrent_execs` | int | `8` | at least 1 |
| `max_transfer_size` | size | `1GB` | the size format of `[server].max_body_size` |
| `log_retention` | duration | `7d` | more than 0 |
| `reconcile_interval` | duration | `1m` | 10 s to 10 m, both included |
| `[[sandbox.profiles]]` | list of tables | | at least one |
| `[[sandbox.credentials]]` | list of tables | none | |

Exactly one way to authenticate to the gateway is configured: mutual TLS (`tls_cert` with `tls_key`), `token_file`, or OIDC client credentials. None, or more than one, is a failure that names `sandbox.gateway_url` and lists the ways found. `tls_ca` may accompany any of the three.

When sandboxes are on, `[server].external_url` must be set; an empty one is a failure that names `server.external_url`.

A valid section is available to the rest of the hub as one read-only value with every default filled in. It does not change while the process runs.

### Profiles and configured credentials (§13.3.2, §13.3.4, SBX-FR-067)

A profile is the operator's template for a sandbox, fixed for the life of the process.

| Field | Type | Default | Valid |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$`, unique among the profiles |
| `default` | bool | false | at most one profile sets it |
| `description` | string | `""` | |
| `image` | string | `""` (the runtime's default image) | |
| `cpu`, `memory` | string | `""` (the runtime's default) | |
| `gpu` | int | 0 | 0 or more |
| `ttl` | duration | required | more than 0 and at most `[sandbox].max_ttl` |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `[sandbox].idle_timeout` | 0 or more |
| `policy` | path | the built-in policy | a readable file |
| `credentials` | list of strings | `[]` | each the `name` of a `[[sandbox.credentials]]` entry |
| `optional_credentials` | list of strings | `[]` | as `credentials`; a name may not be in both lists |
| `expose_secrets` | list of strings | `[]` | the name rules below |
| `optional_expose_secrets` | list of strings | `[]` | the name rules below; a name may not be in both lists |
| `hub_access` | enum | `fork` | `fork` or `none` |
| `env` | map of strings | `{}` | each key matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` and does not start with `PARLEY_` or `OPENSHELL_` |
| `checkpoint` | bool | true | |
| `allow_proposals` | bool | true | |

A configured credential has `name` (required, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$`, unique), `provider_profile` (required, not empty) and `secret` (required, not empty).

Name rules for `expose_secrets` and `optional_expose_secrets` (static half of SBX-FR-067): a name matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`; does not start with `PARLEY_` or `OPENSHELL_`; is not a reserved secret name of §11 (`GIT_PAT`, `GIT_USERNAME`, `GIT_PASSWORD`, `UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT`, `UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME`, `UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD`, `FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, compared without regard to case); is not a key of the profile's `env`; and is not in both lists. Whether the secrets exist is not checked at start.

The loaded profiles can be looked up by name, the default profile can be asked for (there may be none), and all can be listed in name order.

### Start-up runtime check (SBX-FR-003, PLAT-FR-002, §13.7, §13.9)

After static validation, as a start hook that runs before the listener is bound, the hub contacts the runtime once. The whole check has 30 seconds. In this order it:

1. connects and authenticates, and reads the gateway's release;
2. checks that the release is inside the range this hub supports;
3. makes sure the OpenShell workspace `openshell_workspace` exists, creating it when it does not;
4. installs the provider profile of the hub credential, id `parley-hub`: it declares the variable `PARLEY_API_KEY` and authorizes the scheme, host and port of `[server].external_url` for paths under `/api/v1/` and `/git/`, for any program. A profile with that id that already exists is replaced;
5. reads every `provider_profile` named in `[[sandbox.credentials]]`; one the gateway does not know is a failure naming `sandbox.credentials[<name>].provider_profile`. For each sandbox profile, an exposed-secret name that equals a variable declared by a provider profile of one of the profile's `credentials` or `optional_credentials` is a failure naming the profile and the name (start-up half of SBX-FR-067);
6. sends every profile's `policy` file to the runtime for validation; one the runtime rejects, or cannot validate, is a failure naming `sandbox.profiles[<name>].policy` with the runtime's reason. The hosts the runtime reports as allowed are kept for the profile list. The built-in policy is not sent.

The first failure stops the check and the start: exit status 1, one error line on stderr that names the key or the profile, no `listening` line. A gateway that cannot be reached, refuses the credential, or does not answer in time is a failure naming `sandbox.gateway_url`. A release outside the range is a failure whose message holds the connected release and the supported range. The message is scrubbed and never contains the gateway token or the OIDC client secret.

On success the runtime is marked reachable, and `GET /version` carries `sandbox_runtime: {"supported": "<range>", "connected": "<release>"}`: the range as `>=<lowest> <<first unsupported>` and the release read in step 1.

### Runtime client (§13.3.1, SBX-FR-005)

The hub is a client of one OpenShell gateway and owns everything in its OpenShell workspace. All of the hub's traffic to the runtime goes through one client interface, defined in `internal/sandbox/runtime`, with two implementations: one over the OpenShell Go SDK and one in memory for tests. The interface offers these operations, each taking a context:

| Group | Operations |
|---|---|
| Gateway | `Release` (the gateway's health and its release); `EnsureWorkspace`; `Reachable` (the flag below, no call) |
| Provider profiles | `GetProviderProfile` (id, declared variables, authorized hosts); `InstallProviderProfile` (create or replace) |
| Providers | `EnsureProvider` (name, provider profile id, secret value, labels; create or replace); `DeleteProvider`; `AttachProvider` and `DetachProvider` (a provider and a sandbox); `SandboxProviders` (those of one sandbox); `ListProviders` (all of the workspace, with their labels) |
| Policy | `ValidatePolicy` (a policy value; returns the hosts it allows and the provider names its base document refers to); `GetPolicy` (a sandbox's policy and its revision); `AddPolicyRule` (one rule added to a sandbox's policy); `ListProposals` (the pending proposals of the workspace: the runtime's proposal id, the sandbox, the rule, the summary, the findings); `ApproveProposal`; `RejectProposal` |
| Sandboxes | `CreateSandbox` (name, image, cpu, memory, gpu, working directory, environment, policy value, providers, labels); `GetSandbox`; `ListSandboxes` (all of the workspace, with their labels); `DeleteSandbox`; `StopSandbox` (releases the compute, keeps the working directory); `StartSandbox` (with a policy value and an environment); `WaitReady`; `WatchSandboxes` (state changes); `RunMain` (starts the main process of a sandbox from a command) |
| Exec | `Exec` (command, working directory, environment, stdin; collects exit code, stdout and stderr); `ExecStream` (the same, with stdout and stderr delivered as they are produced; the command is killed when the context ends); `ExecInteractive` (a command on a terminal of a given size, with input, output, resize and close) |
| Files | `Upload` (a reader to a path with a mode, creating parent directories); `MakeDir`; `Stat` (file or directory, size, mode); `Download` (a file as a stream); `Walk` (the files and directories below a directory) |
| Logs | `Logs` (the main process's output or the policy log of one sandbox, with since, tail and follow) |

This is the whole interface: packages 45 to 48 call these operations by these names and add none. The types they exchange are plain data:

- **Policy value**: three parts, which the runtime merges: the base document (the content of a profile's `policy` file, or the built-in policy), the protected rules and the added rules. A rule is an object in OpenShell's schema that the hub does not interpret. No base document and no added rule removes or narrows a protected rule; a policy value the runtime refuses is an `invalid` result with the runtime's reason.
- **Sandbox status** (`GetSandbox`, `ListSandboxes`, `WatchSandboxes`): the name, the labels, the state (`pending`, `running`, `restarting`, `stopped`), whether the main process has ended and with which exit code, and whether the runtime still holds the working directory.
- **Log entry** (`Logs`): the time, the source (`process` or `policy`), the stream (`stdout` or `stderr`) and the text of a process line; for a policy entry the action (`allow` or `deny`), program, host, port, method and path (both absent for a connection) and the provider name of a credentialed request.
- **Proposal** (`ListProposals`): the runtime's proposal id, the sandbox name, the rule, the one-line summary and the findings (`severity`, `message`).

What every operation guarantees:

- **Scope.** It acts in the configured OpenShell workspace and in no other.
- **Error kinds.** A failure is one of four kinds, which callers tell apart: `not found` (the runtime has no such sandbox, provider, profile, proposal or path), `invalid` (the runtime understood and refused the request; the runtime's reason is kept), `unsupported` (the SDK in use has no such operation; every operation of the table may answer so, and none is imitated with other calls), and `unavailable` (everything else: the gateway cannot be reached, refuses the hub's credential, answers with a server error, or the call ran out of time).
- **Time.** An operation that does not stream is given at most 30 seconds, or less when the caller's context ends sooner; past it the result is `unavailable`. Streaming operations (`WatchSandboxes`, followed `Logs`, `ExecStream`, `ExecInteractive`, `Upload`, `Download`, `Walk`) end with the caller's context.
- **Reachability.** The client keeps one flag. A call that ends `unavailable` clears it; a call that ends in any other way sets it. It is set by a successful start-up check. Other packages read it for `runtime_reachable`. Every change of the flag is reported to the metrics recorder as `parley_sandbox_runtime_up` 1 or 0.
- **No process exit.** No failure of the runtime ends the hub process once it is listening.
- **No credential in text.** The gateway token and the OIDC client secret are registered with the scrubber when the client is built, and an error's text is scrubbed before it is returned.

The in-memory implementation gives the same results as the SDK implementation for the same sequence of calls, which one set of contract tests proves by running against both. It is the only test double of the runtime in the repository: packages 45 to 48 test against it and do not extend it. It keeps per workspace: provider profiles, providers, sandboxes with their status, the policy values it received, files, log entries and proposals. A sandbox's files are held in memory or, when a test asks for it, in a directory of the host in which `Exec` runs real commands (package 47 runs `git` this way); otherwise exec results are scripted. Its terminal echoes its input. Tests can tell it: to be unreachable; to fail one named operation with a chosen error kind and text; to report a chosen release; to hold provider profiles; to reject every policy value a predicate matches and to report provider names for a base document; to change a sandbox's state, end its main process with a code or drop its working directory; to emit process output and policy log entries; to add a pending proposal; and to break an open stream. It reports the calls it received in order and the streams that are open.

**Metrics recorder.** `internal/sandbox` declares the recorder the sandbox packages report their metrics to: `Add`, `Set` and `Observe`, each with a metric name and a label map and each returning an error, which is the method set of the recorder of package 51 in `internal/metrics`. `parleyd` passes that recorder when it exists; the default records nothing. Packages 44 to 48 report the metrics of §13.7 under exactly these names: `parley_sandbox_runtime_up` (this package), `parley_sandboxes{state}`, `parley_sandbox_creates_total{result}` and `parley_sandbox_seconds` (package 45), `parley_sandbox_exec_total{result}` (package 46), `parley_sandbox_checkpoints_total{result}` (package 47) and `parley_sandbox_denials_total` (package 48).

### Feature check and the runtime-error answer (SBX-FR-001, SBX-FR-005, SBX-FR-010)

Every sandbox route, of this package and of packages 45 to 48, declares the sandbox feature check. The check runs after steps 1 to 4 of the global order (path and method, authentication, rate limit, body size and content type) and before the binding guard, the scope check, workspace access, validation and state. While sandboxes are off it answers HTTP 404 with `error_type` `sandboxes_disabled`. So, with sandboxes off: a request without a credential gets `401 unauthenticated`; a path that does not exist gets `404 not_found`; a body over the limit gets `413`; and every authenticated request to a sandbox route gets `404 sandboxes_disabled`, whatever its scopes and whether or not the workspace exists.

A sandbox route whose handler ends with a runtime error of kind `unavailable` or `unsupported` that it did not handle answers HTTP 502 with `error_type` `sandbox_runtime_error` and a scrubbed message. Packages 46 and 47 give the same answer through a function of this package, with the runtime's text scrubbed of the sandbox's own secret values (package 45) as the message; no other package defines a second answer of this type. Routes that answer from stored state or from configuration (`GET /sandbox-profiles`, `GET /sandboxes`) keep answering 200 while the runtime is unreachable.

### Authorization on workspace sandbox routes (SBX-FR-010, SBX-FR-011, SBX-FR-013, SBX-FR-014)

A route under `/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes…` or `/workspaces/:slug/sandbox-rules…` declares one of two kinds, and the kind fixes its checks in the order feature check, binding guard, PAT scope, workspace access:

| Kind | PAT scope | Workspace need | Routes |
|---|---|---|---|
| read | `sandboxes:read` | read | get, list, logs, file download, proposals list |
| write | `sandboxes:write` | write | everything else, including attach, approve and reject |

The answers are those of the components behind the kind: a PAT without the scope gets `403 insufficient_scope` whether or not the workspace exists; a caller with no access gets `404 not_found` (`workspace not found`); an org member with read-only access gets `403 forbidden` on a write route and passes a read route; an owner and the admin token pass both.

A route may also declare that it needs a user (the create route does, SBX-FR-013). The admin token then gets `403 forbidden` with the message `the admin token cannot create a sandbox`, after workspace access and before the handler validates anything. On every other route the admin token is treated like an owner: it can read, stop and delete any sandbox.

### No widening (SBX-FR-012)

Running a command in a sandbox, attaching to it, or writing a file into it needs a credential that covers the sandbox's hub credential. The handler asks for the decision after it has found the sandbox and before it validates the body. The decision:

- a sandbox without a hub credential (`hub_access` null) is covered by every caller;
- the admin token and an API key cover every hub credential;
- a PAT covers it when it holds every scope in `hub_access.scopes`, by the scope check of package 06, and, when the PAT has a `paths` limit, the sandbox's `hub_access.paths` is not null and each of its globs is covered by one of the PAT's globs, by the cover rule of package 06 (PLAT-FR-059).

A caller that does not cover it gets `403 insufficient_scope`, and nothing is run, attached or written.

### `GET /sandbox-profiles` and `parley sandbox profiles` (SBX-FR-015, §13.5, §13.6)

Lists the hub's profiles. It needs `sandboxes:read` from a PAT and no workspace access: every user with an API key, the admin token and a PAT with the scope may call it, and workspace-bound tokens may too (the allowlist of package 08). The answer is `200` with `{"items": […], "next_cursor": null}`: every profile, ordered by `name`, on one page. The route takes no query parameters.

Each item has `name`, `default`, `description`, `image`, `cpu`, `memory`, `gpu`, `ttl` (the duration as text), `ttl_seconds`, `idle_timeout` (the duration as text; the hub's default when the profile sets none), `policy_summary` (the hosts the base policy allows, sorted; `[]` for the built-in policy), `credentials`, `optional_credentials`, `exposed_secrets` (`[{name, optional}]` sorted by name, `[]` when the profile exposes nothing), `hub_access`, `env_keys` (the keys of `env`, sorted), `checkpoint` and `allow_proposals`. It has no `policy`, `env`, `expose_secrets` or `optional_expose_secrets` member, and no value of an `env` entry or of a secret appears anywhere in the answer.

Errors: `401`; `403 insufficient_scope`; `404 sandboxes_disabled`.

`parley sandbox profiles` calls the route, prints the body on stdout and exits 0; a hub error is printed and exits by the CLI conventions (package 09). `parley sandbox` without a subcommand prints help.

### `GET /sandboxes` (SBX-FR-015, SBX-FR-005, §13.5)

Lists the sandboxes of every workspace, newest first (by `created_at`, then by `id`, both descending), paged by the list convention (`limit` 1 to 200, default 50; `cursor`). Query: `state` (one of `provisioning`, `ready`, `stopped`, `completed`, `failed`, `deleted`) and `user` (the id of the creating user). Filters combine with "and". A `user` that created nothing gives an empty list.

It needs the admin token. Any other credential, including the API key of a user with role `admin` and every PAT, gets `403 forbidden`. An unknown `state`, a `limit` outside 1 to 200 and a cursor that is malformed or from another query are `400 invalid_request`.

The items are sandbox objects, which package 45 defines and stores. This package reads them through a sandbox source, an interface of `internal/sandbox` with one operation `List`: given the filters `state` and `user`, a position (`created_at`, `id`) or none, and a limit, it returns the objects after that position in the order above, each with its `created_at` and `id`. Package 45 implements it over its store and registers it with `RegisterSource`. Until a source is registered the list is empty. The route answers from stored state and never calls the runtime, so it answers 200 while the runtime is unreachable; the source sets each object's `runtime_reachable` from the reachability flag of the runtime client.

Errors: `401`; `403 forbidden`; `400 invalid_request`; `404 sandboxes_disabled`.

### End-to-end flows

**An operator enables sandboxes and a developer lists the profiles.** The operator writes a `[sandbox]` section with a gateway URL, a token file, one credential and one profile, and starts `parleyd`. `parleyd` validates the section, contacts the OpenShell gateway, checks the release, makes sure the workspace exists, installs the `parley-hub` provider profile, checks the credential's provider profile and listens. The developer runs `parley sandbox profiles`; the parley CLI calls `GET /sandbox-profiles`; `parleyd` answers with the profile; the CLI prints it and exits 0. `GET /version` shows the connected release.

**An operator starts the hub against a gateway that is not there.** The operator starts `parleyd` with a valid `[sandbox]` section whose gateway does not answer. `parleyd` validates the section, fails to connect, writes one error line naming `sandbox.gateway_url` and exits 1 without listening.

**An agent asks a hub without sandboxes for the profiles.** The hub runs without a `[sandbox]` section. An agent with a PAT calls `GET /sandbox-profiles`. `parleyd` authenticates it and answers `404 sandboxes_disabled`.

**The gateway goes away while the hub runs.** The hub runs with sandboxes on. The OpenShell gateway stops answering. A call through the runtime client fails as `unavailable` and the client marks the runtime unreachable. The operator calls `GET /sandboxes` with the admin token and `parleyd` answers 200 from stored state; a route that needs the runtime answers `502 sandbox_runtime_error`; the process keeps running.

## Design Decisions

1. **Project decisions relied on.** Go; HTTP on `net/http` with the router of package 02; the CLI on `github.com/spf13/cobra` through package 09; the runtime client is `github.com/ai-openshell/sdk-go` (package `openshell/v1`); tests use the standard `testing` package, table-driven, with `net/http/httptest`; code takes a replaceable clock.
2. **The section is registered as a whole.** Package 03's loader checks one registered key at a time and stops at the first bad one; SBX-FR-002 wants every failure together. This package registers the section `sandbox` with the loader as one entry whose validator receives the parsed section, after environment references are replaced, and returns one error listing every failure, separated by `; `. The registration is package 03's `RegisterSection(name, validator)` in `internal/config/registry.go`, and the loaded section is read through `cfg.Section(name)`; package 03 owns both and this package edits no file of `internal/config` (with package 03). Why: the unknown-key rule and the collect-everything rule then have one owner.
3. **The one error line is cut at 1024 bytes** by the scrubber of package 03 like every start error. Failures are listed in the order of the tables above, so the first ones always survive.
4. **Files are checked for readability at static validation** (`tls_*`, `token_file`, `oidc_client_secret_file`, `policy`). The PRD types them as paths and says nothing; a missing file is a mistake the operator wants reported with the others.
5. **`token_file` is read once, at start,** and its content without surrounding white space is the bearer token for the life of the process. Why: the configuration is read once at start (package 03), and renewal is what the OIDC option is for.
6. **`gateway_url` shape.** No user information, query, fragment or path. "Loopback" means `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8` and `::1`. The same rule applies to `oidc_issuer`, except that an issuer may have a path.
7. **Pattern for `openshell_workspace` and credential names** is the profile name pattern. The PRD gives none.
8. **Lower bounds.** Each `max_…` count is at least 1; `max_ttl`, `max_exec_timeout` and `log_retention` are more than 0. The PRD gives only defaults.
9. **`max_per_org` above `max_sandboxes`.** A `max_per_org` the file sets above `max_sandboxes` is a failure. When the file does not set it, its default is the smaller of 100 and `max_sandboxes`, so lowering `max_sandboxes` alone is not an error.
10. **`[server].external_url` is required with sandboxes on.** A sandbox reaches the hub at that URL (`PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL`) and the hub credential's provider profile authorizes exactly its host. The PRD does not say what happens without it.
11. **A credential name in both `credentials` and `optional_credentials` is a failure,** like an exposed name in both of its lists.
12. **Static name rules of SBX-FR-067 are validated here,** although package 45 owns exposed secrets, because profile validation is one pass that reports everything together. Package 45 owns resolution, missing values and redaction.
13. **The start-up check stops at its first failure.** Later steps need the earlier ones, and SBX-US-01 asks for one message that names the problem.
14. **The supported release range** is one pair in `internal/sandbox/compat.go`: the lowest supported release, included, and the first unsupported release, excluded, compared as semantic versions. They are set from the SDK version in `go.mod`: lowest is that version's `major.minor.0`; first unsupported is the next major, or the next minor while the major is 0. A release that is not a semantic version is outside the range. Why: the PRD says the hub states its range and refuses anything outside it, and gives no numbers.
15. **The hub credential's provider profile** has the fixed id `parley-hub`, is installed at every start whatever the profiles' `hub_access`, and names no program restriction. The per-workspace narrowing of the hub rule belongs to the sandbox's policy (packages 45 and 48).
16. **A runtime that cannot validate a policy fails the start** for a profile that names a `policy` file (the client's `unsupported` kind is treated like a rejection). Why: starting with a policy nobody checked would break "refuses to start if the runtime rejects it". The built-in policy is the hub's own and is not sent.
17. **Layout inside `internal/sandbox`.** The interface is in `internal/sandbox/runtime`, the SDK implementation in `…/runtime/openshell`, the fake and the contract tests in `…/runtime/runtimetest` (as `internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest` does for origins). Only `…/runtime/openshell` imports the SDK.
18. **Error kinds and the 30-second bound** on non-streaming calls are this package's. The PRD names only `502 sandbox_runtime_error`; callers need to tell "no such sandbox" from "no gateway".
19. **An SDK without an operation.** Sandbox stop and start are described by OpenShell's documentation but were not confirmed in the SDK, and a call that validates a policy value, the policy value in three parts, `AddPolicyRule`, `RunMain`, `Stat`, `MakeDir` and `Walk` are not in the SDK's documented surface. The interface declares them all. Where the SDK in `go.mod` has no call that does what an operation says, the implementation returns the `unsupported` kind and does not imitate the operation with others; a caller that gets `unsupported` answers `502 sandbox_runtime_error` or fails its sandbox, as its own package says.
20. **Reachability has no probe of its own.** The flag follows the calls other packages make (reconciliation runs every minute, package 47).
21. **The hub composition takes a runtime factory** (configuration in, client out) whose default builds the SDK implementation, so that tests and `test/e2e` start a hub with the SDK implementation over the SDK's in-memory fake client, or with the fake of this package.
22. **`GET /sandbox-profiles` is one page** with `next_cursor` null and no query parameters. Profiles are configuration and few; the CLI entry has no paging flags.
23. **Profile list details.** `policy_summary` is an array of host strings. `image`, `cpu` and `memory` are `""` when the profile leaves them to the runtime. `ttl` and `idle_timeout` are written in the largest unit that divides them (`4h`, `30m`, `0s`).
24. **`GET /sandboxes` reads through a source that package 45 registers,** because the sandbox object and its storage are that package's while the route is this one's. `user` is a user id. A PAT gets `403 forbidden` from the admin check; the route declares no scope.
25. **Non-PAT credentials cover every hub credential** in the no-widening decision: an API key holds every scope and has no `paths`, and the admin token is not scope-checked. A PAT with `paths` does not cover a sandbox whose hub credential has none.
26. **The no-widening decision runs after the sandbox lookup and before body validation;** the user-only rule runs after workspace access. Both are authorization and so precede validation in the order of SBX-FR-010.
27. **Dependency on package 09** is added to the plan's list because this package specifies a `parley` command (brief, note on CLI commands).
28. **Profile: full**, with four execution paths.
29. **The interface is complete for packages 45 to 48.** Those packages were written to "add what is missing" to the client; instead this package declares every operation they call (the table of "Runtime client"), with the fake's test controls, and they use the names of this package and touch neither the interface, the OpenShell implementation nor the fake. Why: four packages extending one interface in parallel would each define it differently. The operations come from their needs: providers, creation in a working directory, `RunMain` and the environment (45); `ExecStream`, `ExecInteractive`, the file operations and `Logs` (46); `StopSandbox`, `StartSandbox`, the status with the main process's end and the working directory, `ListSandboxes` and `ListProviders` with labels (47); the policy value in three parts, `ValidatePolicy` with the providers a base document refers to, `AddPolicyRule`, `ListProposals`, `RejectProposal` and the policy source of `Logs` for denials (48).
30. **Sandbox metrics go through one recorder interface declared here.** Package 51 owns the catalogue and its recorder and expects each feature package to report to it; no sandbox package depends on package 51. The interface has the recorder's method set, each method returning an error as the registry methods of package 51 do, so `parleyd` passes the registry of `internal/metrics` without an adapter. This package reports `parley_sandbox_runtime_up` on every change of the reachability flag.

## Dependencies

- Package 03 server_lifecycle_and_configuration (draft): the configuration loader and its registry, the start hooks, the scrubber, the hub composition in `internal/hub`.
- Package 07 workspace_access_rule (draft): the access decision for a declared need; through it, packages 02 (router, check positions, error envelope, lists), 04 (the caller's credential type), 05 and 06 (scope check, cover rule).
- Package 09 cli_foundation (draft): the HTTP client, output, exit codes and command declaration for `parley sandbox profiles`.
- OpenShell: one gateway of a supported release, reached through `github.com/ai-openshell/sdk-go`.

## Verified External API

`github.com/ai-openshell/sdk-go`, package `openshell/v1`. Nothing below was read in source; every symbol is **unverified** and recorded with `"verified": false`. The documented surface:

- `v1.NewClient(v1.Config{Address, Auth, TLS})`; auth helpers `v1.StaticToken`, `v1.RefreshableToken` and the `oidc` sub-package.
- `Sandboxes()`: create, get, list, delete, watch, `WaitReady`, logs, provider attach, detach and list. Not confirmed: starting a main process after creation (`RunMain`), a working directory at creation, and the status members for the main process's end and the working directory.
- `Exec()`: `Run`, stream, interactive.
- `Files()`: upload, download. Not confirmed: `Stat`, `MakeDir` and `Walk`.
- `Providers()`: create, read, update, delete, ensure; `.Profiles()`: list, get, import, update, lint, delete.
- `Policy()`: draft review, approve, reject, merge, status. Not confirmed: a policy value in three parts and `AddPolicyRule`.
- `Workspaces()`.
- `Health()`: health, gateway info.
- package `fake`: an in-memory client.

Not confirmed:

- **Sandbox stop and start**: described in OpenShell's documentation, not confirmed in the SDK. Assumed to be operations of `Sandboxes()`. If absent, design decision 19 applies.
- **Validation of a policy document without a sandbox**: **NOT FOUND** in the documented surface. Assumed to be an operation of `Policy()` that returns the runtime's verdict and the hosts the policy allows. If absent, design decisions 16 and 19 apply.
- The exact method names, parameter types and error types of every operation above, and the module version, which is set when the module is added to `go.mod`.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Scope / permission**: A string carried by a PAT that grants read or write access to an area.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it). A token bound to a fork also reaches its own changes, and the awareness and policy reads, on the fork's parent (§3).
- **Path-scoped token**: A PAT whose writes are limited to files matching a list of globs.
- **Sandbox**: An isolated environment in which an agent runs, attached to a workspace (normally a task fork) and started with it checked out. It runs on OpenShell; the hub controls it (§13).
- **OpenShell**: The open-source sandbox runtime Parley's sandboxes run on. It provides the isolation, the policy format and the credential mechanism. The hub is a client of one OpenShell gateway.
- **Profile**: The operator's template for a sandbox, defined in configuration: image, resources, time limits, base policy, credentials and the secrets it exposes.
- **Exposed secret**: A secret (§11) that a profile names in `expose_secrets`. Its real value is placed in the sandbox's environment, where code in the sandbox can read it. Off unless the operator lists the secret (§13).
- **Credential (sandbox)**: A secret (§11) attached to a sandbox as an OpenShell provider. The workload sees only a placeholder; the runtime adds the real value outside the sandbox, on requests to the endpoints the provider's profile authorizes.
- **Hub credential**: The fork-bound PAT the hub mints for a sandbox so that it can reach the hub. The workload sees only its placeholder, in `PARLEY_API_KEY`.
- **Provider profile**: OpenShell's definition of how a credential may be used: the environment variable that holds its placeholder, and the hosts, ports, paths and programs it is added for.
- **Runtime**: The OpenShell gateway the hub is configured with, and the one OpenShell workspace in it that the hub owns.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Feature switch and static validation of [sandbox]

**Rationale:** An operator who mistypes a key must learn of every mistake in one start, and a hub without the section must behave as if sandboxes did not exist.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN the configuration is loaded and the file has no [sandbox] section, THE sandbox configuration SHALL report sandboxes as off, build no runtime client, and let the hub start without contacting any gateway and without changing stored sandbox records
   → the loaded sandbox configuration reports enabled == false; the hub reaches 'listening'; the runtime factory is never called; GET /version has no sandbox_runtime member
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub composed with a counting runtime factory
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/config_test.go and internal/hub/hub_test.go: cfg = load(file without [sandbox]); assert sandbox.FromConfig(cfg).Enabled == false; start a hub with a runtime factory that counts its calls; assert the hub listens; assert factoryCalls == 0; assert 'sandbox_runtime' not in get('/version').json
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN the configuration is loaded and its [sandbox] section sets only gateway_url, one way to authenticate and one profile with name and ttl, with [server].external_url set, THE sandbox configuration SHALL accept the section and fill every other key with its default
   → enabled == true; runtime 'openshell'; openshell_workspace 'parley'; max_ttl 24h; idle_timeout 30m; max_sandboxes 200; max_per_org 100; max_per_workspace 50; max_per_user 20; allow_workspace_rules true; max_exec_timeout 30m; max_concurrent_execs 8; max_transfer_size 1073741824 bytes; log_retention 168h; reconcile_interval 1m; no credentials; a file value replaces its default, and ${NAME} references in string values are replaced before validation
   Check: unit
   - setup: a configuration file whose [sandbox] section has gateway_url https://gw.test:8443, a readable non-empty token_file, [server].external_url set, and one profile {name 'agent', ttl '4h'}
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/config_test.go: s = loadSandbox(minimal file); assert each field equals the default listed in the contract; s2 = loadSandbox(file setting max_sandboxes = 10, reconcile_interval = '10s', gateway_url = '${GW}' with GW set); assert s2.MaxSandboxes == 10; assert s2.ReconcileInterval == 10s; assert s2.GatewayURL == value of GW
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF the [sandbox] section holds one or more invalid values among: runtime other than 'openshell'; gateway_url missing, not a URL, http to a host that is not localhost, 127.0.0.0/8 or ::1, or with user information, a query, a fragment or a path other than '/'; openshell_workspace not matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$; max_ttl, max_exec_timeout or log_retention of 0 or less; idle_timeout below 0; max_sandboxes, max_per_org, max_per_workspace, max_per_user or max_concurrent_execs below 1; max_transfer_size not a size; reconcile_interval below 10s or above 10m; a value of the wrong type; a tls_cert, tls_key, tls_ca, token_file or oidc_client_secret_file that cannot be read; a token_file or oidc_client_secret_file that is empty after trimming white space, THEN THE sandbox configuration SHALL refuse the whole configuration and report every failure of the section together, each naming its key as sandbox.<key>
   → the load returns no configuration and one error whose text contains sandbox.<key> for every invalid key of the case, the failures separated by '; '; with three invalid keys the text names all three; parleyd exits with status 1 and one error line on stderr and writes no 'listening' line; reconcile_interval of exactly 10s and exactly 10m, and http://127.0.0.1:8080 and http://localhost:8080 as gateway_url, are accepted
   Check: unit
   - setup: a configuration file whose [sandbox] section has gateway_url https://gw.test:8443, a readable non-empty token_file, [server].external_url set, and one profile {name 'agent', ttl '4h'}
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/config_test.go, a table with one row per invalid value named in the condition plus the boundary rows of the contract: err = loadSandbox(valid file with the row's change); assert err contains 'sandbox.' + row.key (or err == nil for a boundary row); one more row sets runtime = 'docker', max_ttl = '0s' and reconcile_interval = '5s' together: assert err contains 'sandbox.runtime' and 'sandbox.max_ttl' and 'sandbox.reconcile_interval'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF the [sandbox] section, a [[sandbox.profiles]] table or a [[sandbox.credentials]] table holds a key that is not defined for it, THEN THE sandbox configuration SHALL report the unknown key as a failure together with every other failure of the section
   → the load returns no configuration and an error containing sandbox.<key>, sandbox.profiles[<name>].<key> or sandbox.credentials[<name>].<key> for the unknown key; when the same file also has an invalid value, the error names both
   Check: unit
   - setup: a configuration file whose [sandbox] section has gateway_url https://gw.test:8443, a readable non-empty token_file, [server].external_url set, and one profile {name 'agent', ttl '4h'}
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/config_test.go, a table over {sandbox.gatway_url, sandbox.profiles[agent].imge, sandbox.credentials[model].secrt}: err = loadSandbox(valid file plus the misspelled key); assert err contains row.name; one row adds max_ttl = '0s' as well: assert err contains both names
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF the section configures no way to authenticate to the gateway, or more than one of mutual TLS (tls_cert with tls_key), token_file and OIDC client credentials, or only one of tls_cert and tls_key, or one or two of oidc_issuer, oidc_client_id and oidc_client_secret_file, THEN THE sandbox configuration SHALL refuse the configuration with a failure that names the keys concerned
   → the error contains sandbox.gateway_url and the list of ways found (none, or for example 'mutual TLS, token_file') when the count of ways is not one; it contains sandbox.tls_cert or sandbox.tls_key for an incomplete pair and the missing sandbox.oidc_… keys for an incomplete triple; tls_ca together with exactly one way is accepted
   Check: unit
   - setup: a configuration file whose [sandbox] section has gateway_url https://gw.test:8443, a readable non-empty token_file, [server].external_url set, and one profile {name 'agent', ttl '4h'}, with the files of every row present in t.TempDir()
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/config_test.go, a table over {no auth, token_file + tls pair, token_file + oidc triple, tls_cert alone, tls_key alone, oidc_issuer alone, issuer + client_id, token_file + tls_ca (valid), tls pair + tls_ca (valid)}: err = loadSandbox(row); assert err contains every key the row expects, or err == nil for the valid rows
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] THE sandbox configuration SHALL for any [sandbox] section that fails validation, produce a message that contains neither the content of token_file, nor the content of oidc_client_secret_file, nor the user information of a URL value
   → the error text of a failing load contains none of: the token file's content, the client secret file's content, the text between '://' and '@' of gateway_url or oidc_issuer
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/config_test.go, a table over failing files that also carry a token file with content 'tok-SECRET-1', a secret file with content 'oidc-SECRET-2' and gateway_url 'https://u:pw-SECRET-3@gw.test': err = loadSandbox(row); assert err != nil; assert err contains none of 'tok-SECRET-1', 'oidc-SECRET-2', 'pw-SECRET-3'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] IF the file has a [sandbox] section and [server].external_url is empty, THEN THE sandbox configuration SHALL refuse the configuration with a failure that names server.external_url, reported together with the other failures of the section
   → the load returns no configuration and an error containing server.external_url; the same file without the [sandbox] section loads
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/config_test.go: err = load(valid sandbox file with external_url removed); assert err contains 'server.external_url'; assert load(same file without [sandbox]) succeeds
   ```
1. [REQ-1.8] IF the file sets max_per_org above max_sandboxes, THEN THE sandbox configuration SHALL refuse the configuration with a failure that names sandbox.max_per_org; when the file does not set max_per_org, use the smaller of 100 and max_sandboxes instead of failing
   → max_sandboxes = 50 with max_per_org = 60 fails with an error containing sandbox.max_per_org; max_sandboxes = 50 alone loads with max_per_org == 50; max_sandboxes = 50 with max_per_org = 50 loads; max_sandboxes = 500 alone loads with max_per_org == 100
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/config_test.go, a table over the four cases of the contract: s, err = loadSandbox(row); assert the row's error or the row's MaxPerOrg
   ```

### REQ-2: Profiles and configured credentials

**Rationale:** Agents get sandboxes only of shapes the operator declared, so a profile that is wrong must never reach a running hub.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a valid [sandbox] section is loaded, THE sandbox configuration SHALL make each profile available by name with its defaults filled in, the default profile available on request, and all profiles listable in name order, unchanged for the life of the process
   → a profile that sets only name and ttl has default false, description '', image '', cpu '', memory '', gpu 0, idle_timeout equal to [sandbox].idle_timeout, no policy file (the built-in policy), credentials [], optional_credentials [], expose_secrets [], optional_expose_secrets [], hub_access 'fork', env {}, checkpoint true, allow_proposals true; lookup of an unknown name reports 'no such profile' as a result; the default lookup reports 'no default' when no profile sets default; the list is sorted by name; each configured credential is available by name with provider_profile and secret
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go: s = loadSandbox(file with profiles 'b' {ttl 1h}, 'a' {ttl 2h, default true, idle_timeout '0s', credentials ['model']} and credential model); assert names(s.Profiles()) == ['a','b']; assert s.Profile('b') has every default of the contract; assert s.Profile('a').IdleTimeout == 0; assert s.DefaultProfile().Name == 'a'; assert s.Profile('zz') not found; assert s.Credential('model') == {provider_profile, secret}; with no default set: assert s.DefaultProfile() reports none
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF the section has no profile, or a profile has: no name or a name not matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$; a name another profile has; default true while another profile sets it; no ttl, a ttl of 0 or less, or a ttl above [sandbox].max_ttl; an idle_timeout below 0; a gpu below 0; a hub_access other than 'fork' and 'none'; a policy file that cannot be read, THEN THE sandbox configuration SHALL refuse the configuration and report each failure with the key sandbox.profiles[<name>].<key>, using the profile's zero-based index when it has no usable name, together with every other failure of the section
   → the error contains sandbox.profiles for a section without profiles and sandbox.profiles[<name or index>].<key> for each failing field; a name of 63 characters and a ttl equal to max_ttl are accepted; a name of 64 characters and a ttl one second above max_ttl are refused; two profiles with default true are refused with an error naming the second one's default
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go, a table with one row per failure named in the condition and the four boundary rows of the contract: err = loadSandbox(valid file with the row's change); assert err contains row.key, or err == nil for an accepted boundary; one row breaks ttl of profile 'a' and hub_access of profile 'b': assert err contains 'sandbox.profiles[a].ttl' and 'sandbox.profiles[b].hub_access'
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF a [[sandbox.credentials]] entry has no name, a name not matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$, a name another entry has, an empty provider_profile or an empty secret; or a profile's credentials or optional_credentials names an entry that does not exist; or one name is in both of a profile's two credential lists, THEN THE sandbox configuration SHALL refuse the configuration and report each failure with its key
   → the error contains sandbox.credentials[<name or index>].<key> for a failing entry, and sandbox.profiles[<name>].credentials or sandbox.profiles[<name>].optional_credentials together with the offending credential name for a failing reference
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go, a table over {entry without name, name 'Bad Name', duplicate name, provider_profile '', secret '', profile references 'nope' in credentials, in optional_credentials, 'model' in both lists}: err = loadSandbox(row); assert err contains row.key and, for a reference row, the credential name
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] IF a key of a profile's env does not match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ or starts with PARLEY_ or OPENSHELL_, THEN THE sandbox configuration SHALL refuse the configuration with a failure naming sandbox.profiles[<name>].env and the key
   → the error contains sandbox.profiles[<name>].env and the offending key; the keys PARLEYX, parley_lower and _X are accepted; the error text does not contain the value of the entry
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go, a table over env keys {'PARLEY_X', 'OPENSHELL_Y', '1ABC', 'A-B', '' (refused); 'PARLEYX', 'parley_lower', '_X' (accepted)} each with value 'val-SECRETISH': err = loadSandbox(row); refused rows: assert err contains 'sandbox.profiles[agent].env' and the key and not 'val-SECRETISH'; accepted rows: assert err == nil
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] IF a name in a profile's expose_secrets or optional_expose_secrets does not match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$, starts with PARLEY_ or OPENSHELL_, equals without regard to case one of GIT_PAT, GIT_USERNAME, GIT_PASSWORD, UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT, UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME, UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD or FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, is a key of the profile's env, or is in both lists, THEN THE sandbox configuration SHALL refuse the configuration with a failure naming the profile's list key and the name, without checking whether any secret exists
   → the error contains sandbox.profiles[<name>].expose_secrets or sandbox.profiles[<name>].optional_expose_secrets and the offending name; a profile with expose_secrets ['NPM_TOKEN'] and optional_expose_secrets ['PIP_TOKEN'] loads although no such secret is stored
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go, a table over {'1TOKEN', 'A-B', 'PARLEY_TOKEN', 'OPENSHELL_X', 'GIT_PAT', 'git_pat', 'FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET', a name that is also an env key, a name in both lists} for each of the two lists: err = loadSandbox(row); assert err contains the list key and the name; the valid row of the contract: assert err == nil
   ```

### REQ-3: Start-up runtime check

**Rationale:** A hub that starts against a gateway it cannot use would accept sandbox requests it can never serve.

#### Criteria

1. ### REQ-4: Runtime client

**Rationale:** Packages 45 to 48 drive sandboxes through one client, so its scope, its error kinds and its test double must be fixed before they are written.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] THE runtime client SHALL for any operation of the client interface (gateway, provider profiles, providers, policy, sandboxes, exec, files, logs), act in the configured OpenShell workspace and in no other
   → a sandbox, provider or provider profile created through the client exists in the workspace named by openshell_workspace and is not visible to a client configured with another workspace; a sandbox list returns only sandboxes of the configured workspace
   Check: integration
   - setup: the OpenShell implementation over the SDK's in-memory fake client, and the fake of this package, each as one backend shared by two clients

   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN an operation fails, THE runtime client SHALL return an error of exactly one of four kinds that a caller can test for: not found when the runtime has no such sandbox, provider, provider profile, proposal or path; invalid when the runtime understood and refused the request, keeping the runtime's reason; unsupported when the SDK in use has no such operation; unavailable for every other failure, including a gateway that cannot be reached, a refused hub credential and a server error of the gateway
   → errors.Is(err, runtime.ErrNotFound), ErrInvalid, ErrUnsupported or ErrUnavailable is true for exactly one of the four; an invalid error's text contains the runtime's reason; every operation the SDK has no call for (StopSandbox, StartSandbox, ValidatePolicy, AddPolicyRule, RunMain, Stat, MakeDir and Walk are the candidates) returns ErrUnsupported and is never imitated with other calls
   Check: unit

   in internal/sandbox/runtime/openshell/errors_test.go and runtimetest/contract.go, a table over {get of an unknown sandbox -> not found, delete of an unknown provider -> not found, get of an unknown provider profile -> not found, Stat of a missing path -> not found, validate of a policy the backend rejects with reason 'bad rule' -> invalid and text contains 'bad rule', create with an image reference the backend refuses -> invalid, backend connection refused -> unavailable, backend answers unauthenticated -> unavailable, backend answers a server error -> unavailable, an operation the backend lacks -> unsupported}: err = op(); assert exactly one of the four errors.Is holds and it is the row's
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN an operation ends, THE runtime client SHALL clear the reachability flag when it ended with kind unavailable and set it when it ended in any other way, a success and the kinds not found, invalid and unsupported included, and report every change of the flag to the metrics recorder
   → Reachable() is false after an unavailable result and true after the next result of any other kind; it is safe to read while operations run in other goroutines; the hub process does not exit on any result; the recorder received parley_sandbox_runtime_up 0 when the flag was cleared and 1 when it was set again, once per change

   ```

   → HTTP 404 with error_type sandboxes_disabled for GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles, GET /api/v1/sandboxes and a workspace sandbox route, for the admin token, an API key, a PAT with sandboxes:read, a PAT without any sandbox scope, on an existing workspace and on a slug that does not exist; the handler is not called
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real router with authentication, the scope check and workspace access installed, against a real store holding workspace 'ws'

   → a request without a credential to a sandbox route gets HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated; a path that no route has gets HTTP 404 with error_type not_found; a method the route does not have gets HTTP 405 with error_type method_not_allowed; a JSON body over the body limit sent to a sandbox route gets HTTP 413
   Check: integration

1. [REQ-5.3] WHILE sandboxes are on, THE parleyd SHALL pass the feature check on every route that declares it and leave the answer to the later checks and the handler
   → the probe route's handler is called for a caller who passes the later checks; a PAT without the scope gets HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope and not sandboxes_disabled

### REQ-7: No widening through a sandbox

**Rationale:** A weak token must not act through a sandbox that a stronger credential created.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN a handler asks whether a PAT covers a sandbox's hub credential, THE no-widening decision SHALL answer yes only when the PAT holds every scope in the hub credential's scopes, by the scope check of package 06, and either the PAT has no paths limit, or the hub credential has a paths limit and each of its globs is covered by one of the PAT's globs by the cover rule of package 06
   → covered: PAT scopes include all of hub_access.scopes and (PAT paths null, or hub_access.paths non-null and every glob covered); not covered: one scope missing; PAT paths set and hub_access.paths null; one hub glob that no PAT glob covers
   Check: unit

   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] WHEN a handler asks whether the admin token or an API key covers a sandbox's hub credential, or whether any caller covers a sandbox that has no hub credential, THE no-widening decision SHALL answer yes
   → Covers is true for the admin token and for an API key against any scopes and paths, and for every credential type when the sandbox's hub_access is null
   Check: unit

   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] IF a caller that does not cover the sandbox's hub credential calls a route that runs a command in the sandbox, attaches to it or writes a file into it, THEN THE no-widening decision SHALL refuse the request after the sandbox was found and before the body is validated, and run, attach or write nothing
   → HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope; the rest of the handler does not run and the runtime receives no call; a covering caller on the same route reaches the rest of the handler

   ```

### REQ-8: Profile list over REST and the CLI

**Rationale:** An agent has to know which profile to ask for, and must learn it without seeing a policy path, an environment value or a secret.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN a caller with an API key, the admin token or a PAT holding sandboxes:read requests GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles while sandboxes are on, THE parleyd SHALL return every profile on one page, ordered by name, without requiring access to any workspace and whatever query parameters the request carries
   → HTTP 200 with body {items: [...], next_cursor: null}; items are sorted by name ascending and hold one object per configured profile; a user who owns no workspace and is in no organization gets the same list; the answer is the same while the runtime is unreachable
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub with sandboxes on, the fake runtime, and profiles 'plain' and 'agent' configured in that order
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/routes_test.go: a table over {API key of a user with no workspace, admin token, PAT [sandboxes:read]}: r = get('/sandbox-profiles', cred); assert r.status == 200; assert names(r.json.items) == ['agent','plain']; assert r.json.next_cursor == null; assert get('/sandbox-profiles?limit=1&cursor=x', cred).json.items has 2 entries; rt.SetUnreachable(true): assert status still 200
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any profile in the list, show name, default, description, image, cpu, memory, gpu, ttl, ttl_seconds, idle_timeout, policy_summary, credentials, optional_credentials, exposed_secrets, hub_access, env_keys, checkpoint and allow_proposals, and show no policy path, no env value, no expose_secrets or optional_expose_secrets member and no secret value
   → for a profile with ttl 4h, idle_timeout unset under a hub default of 30m, env {B: 'vb', A: 'va'}, expose_secrets ['Z_TOKEN'], optional_expose_secrets ['A_TOKEN'], a policy file for which the runtime reported hosts ['b.test','a.test']: ttl == '4h', ttl_seconds == 14400, idle_timeout == '30m', env_keys == ['A','B'], exposed_secrets == [{name:'A_TOKEN',optional:true},{name:'Z_TOKEN',optional:false}], policy_summary == ['a.test','b.test']; the item has no members policy, env, expose_secrets, optional_expose_secrets; the body contains neither 'va' nor 'vb' nor the policy file's path; a profile with the built-in policy and nothing exposed has policy_summary == [] and exposed_secrets == [], and image, cpu and memory '' when unset
   Check: integration
   - setup: the configuration of the contract, with the fake runtime reporting the two hosts for the policy file
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/routes_test.go: item = find(get('/sandbox-profiles').json.items, 'agent'); assert each member as in the contract; assert keys(item) == the eighteen member names of the action; assert body contains none of 'va', 'vb', policyPath; plain = find(items, 'plain'); assert plain.policy_summary == [] and plain.exposed_secrets == [] and plain.image == ''
   ```
1. [REQ-8.3] IF a PAT that does not hold sandboxes:read requests GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles while sandboxes are on, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope and no profile data in the body; a request without a credential gets HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/routes_test.go: r = get('/sandbox-profiles', PAT [workspaces:read]); assert r.status == 403; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'insufficient_scope'; assert 'items' not in r.json; assert get('/sandbox-profiles', no credential).status == 401
   ```
1. [REQ-8.4] WHEN a user runs parley sandbox profiles with a hub URL and a credential, THE parley CLI SHALL call GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles once, print the response body on stdout as one JSON document and exit 0; print a hub error as its envelope on stderr and exit with the status the CLI conventions give it
   → against a hub with sandboxes on: exit status 0, stdout is the JSON document {items, next_cursor} indented by 2 spaces, stderr empty; against a hub with sandboxes off: stdout empty, stderr holds the envelope with error_type sandboxes_disabled, exit status 1; parley sandbox without a subcommand prints help listing profiles and exits 0 without a credential
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/cli/sandbox_test.go, against an httptest hub stub: code, out, errOut = run('sandbox','profiles'); assert code == 0; assert json(out).items[0].name == 'agent'; assert request path == '/api/v1/sandbox-profiles' and method GET, sent once; with the stub answering 404 sandboxes_disabled: assert code == 1; assert out == ''; assert json(errOut).error.error_type == 'sandboxes_disabled'; run('sandbox') without settings: assert code == 0 and out contains 'profiles'
   ```

### REQ-9: Hub-wide sandbox list for the admin token

**Rationale:** An operator needs one view of every sandbox on the hub, also while the runtime is down.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-9.1] WHEN the admin token requests GET /api/v1/sandboxes while sandboxes are on, THE parleyd SHALL return the sandbox objects of every workspace that the registered sandbox source holds, newest first by created_at and then by id, both descending, paged by limit and cursor, without calling the runtime
   → HTTP 200 with {items, next_cursor}; with 5 stored sandboxes in 3 workspaces and limit=2, three requests following next_cursor return 2, 2 and 1 items, each sandbox once, in descending created_at order with ties broken by descending id, and the last next_cursor is null; without limit all 5 are on one page; the runtime fake records no call; each item is the object the source returned, member for member
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub with sandboxes on, the fake runtime, and an in-memory sandbox source registered that holds 5 objects in 3 workspaces, two of them with the same created_at
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/routes_test.go: r1 = get('/sandboxes?limit=2', admin); r2 = get('/sandboxes?limit=2&cursor=' + r1.json.next_cursor, admin); r3 = same with r2's cursor; assert ids(r1 + r2 + r3) == the five ids in the expected order; assert r3.json.next_cursor == null; assert rt.Calls() == []; assert get('/sandboxes', admin).json.items has 5 entries
   ```
1. [REQ-9.2] WHEN the request carries state, user or both, THE parleyd SHALL return only the sandboxes in that state and created by the user with that id, the two filters combined with 'and'
   → state=ready returns exactly the stored sandboxes in state ready; user=<id> returns exactly those that user created; both together return the intersection; a user id that created none returns HTTP 200 with items [] and next_cursor null; a cursor obtained with one filter and sent with another is HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request
   Check: integration
   - setup: the source of the criterion above, its objects in states ready, ready, stopped, deleted, failed, created by users u1 and u2
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/routes_test.go, a table over {state=ready, state=deleted, user=u1, state=ready&user=u1, user=nobody}: r = get('/sandboxes?' + q, admin); assert ids(r.json.items) == expected(q); c = get('/sandboxes?state=ready&limit=1', admin).json.next_cursor; assert get('/sandboxes?state=stopped&cursor=' + c, admin).status == 400
   ```
1. [REQ-9.3] IF a credential other than the admin token requests GET /api/v1/sandboxes while sandboxes are on, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without reading any sandbox
   → HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden for the API key of a user with role admin, the API key of any other user, and a PAT with sandboxes:read and sandboxes:write; the sandbox source is not called; without a credential HTTP 401
   Check: integration

   in internal/sandbox/routes_test.go, a table over {API key of a role-admin user, API key of a plain user, PAT [sandboxes:read, sandboxes:write]}: r = get('/sandboxes', cred); assert r.status == 403; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'forbidden'; assert sourceCalls == 0; assert get('/sandboxes', none).status == 401
   ```
1. [REQ-9.4] IF the request carries a state outside provisioning, ready, stopped, completed, failed and deleted, a limit outside 1 to 200 or not a number, or a cursor that is malformed, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without reading any sandbox
   → HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request; limit=1 and limit=200 are accepted; the sandbox source is not called for a refused request

   ```
1. [REQ-9.5] WHILE sandboxes are on and no sandbox source is registered, THE parleyd SHALL answer the admin token's GET /api/v1/sandboxes with an empty list

   Check: integration

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An operator enables sandboxes and a developer lists the profiles

1. **operator** writes a [sandbox] section with a gateway URL, a token file, one credential and one profile, and starts parleyd
2. **parleyd** validates the section and fills the defaults
3. **parleyd** connects to the OpenShell gateway with the token and asks for its release
4. **OpenShell gateway** answers with a release inside the supported range
5. **parleyd** makes sure its OpenShell workspace exists, installs the provider profile parley-hub and reads the credential's provider profile
6. **OpenShell gateway** holds the workspace and the provider profile afterwards
7. **parleyd** binds the listener and logs 'listening'
8. **developer** runs parley sandbox profiles
9. **parley CLI** calls GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles with the developer's credential
10. **parleyd** answers 200 with the profile, without its policy path or env values
11. **parley CLI** prints the list on stdout and exits 0

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** configuration loader, hub start sequence and start hooks, sandbox configuration and start-up check, OpenShell runtime client implementation, HTTP router with authentication and scope check, parley CLI

**Setup:**

- the hub is started in-process with the default runtime factory replaced by one that builds the OpenShell implementation over the SDK's in-memory fake client, which holds the provider profile 'anthropic'
- a config.toml in t.TempDir() with [server].external_url, a [sandbox] section using token_file, credential model -> anthropic and profile 'agent' {ttl '4h', credentials ['model'], env {A: 'va'}}
- a signed-in developer with an API key

**End state:**

- the SDK's in-memory client holds the workspace 'parley' and the provider profile 'parley-hub'
- parley sandbox profiles exits 0 and prints one item named 'agent' with env_keys ['A'] and no member 'env'
- GET /version carries sandbox_runtime.connected equal to the fake's release

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/sandbox_runtime_test.go: hub = startHub(cfg, runtimeFactory(sdkFake)); assert sdkFake has workspace 'parley' and profile 'parley-hub'; code, out = parley('sandbox','profiles'); assert code == 0; assert json(out).items[0].name == 'agent'; assert 'va' not in out; assert get('/version').json.sandbox_runtime.connected == sdkFake.release
```

### PATH-2: An operator starts the hub against a gateway that is not there

1. **operator** starts parleyd with a valid [sandbox] section whose gateway_url points at a port nobody listens on
2. **parleyd** validates the section
3. **parleyd** tries to connect to the OpenShell gateway and fails
4. **parleyd** writes one error line naming sandbox.gateway_url and exits with status 1 without binding the listener
5. **operator** reads the line and finds the key to correct

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** configuration loader, hub start sequence and start hooks, sandbox start-up check, OpenShell runtime client implementation with the default runtime factory

**Setup:**

- a config.toml whose gateway_url is http://127.0.0.1:<a port that was just closed> with a token_file holding 'gw-tok-SECRET'

**End state:**

- parleyd has exited with status 1
- stderr holds exactly one line; it contains 'sandbox.gateway_url' and does not contain 'gw-tok-SECRET'
- no 'listening' line was written and no connection to the hub's port is accepted

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/sandbox_runtime_test.go: status, stderr = runHub(cfg); assert status == 1; assert lines(stderr) == 1; assert 'sandbox.gateway_url' in stderr; assert 'gw-tok-SECRET' not in stderr; assert 'listening' not in stderr
```

### PATH-3: An agent asks a hub without sandboxes for the profiles

1. **operator** runs parleyd with a configuration that has no [sandbox] section
2. **parleyd** starts without contacting any gateway
3. **agent** calls GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles with a PAT that holds sandboxes:read
4. **parleyd** authenticates the PAT, finds sandboxes off and answers 404 with error_type sandboxes_disabled
5. **agent** learns that this hub offers no sandboxes

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** configuration loader, hub start sequence, HTTP router with authentication, sandbox feature check

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process without a [sandbox] section, with a runtime factory that fails the test when called
- a user with a PAT holding sandboxes:read

**End state:**

- the response is 404 with error_type sandboxes_disabled
- the runtime factory was never called
- GET /version has no sandbox_runtime member

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/sandbox_runtime_test.go: hub = startHub(cfgWithoutSandbox, failingFactory); r = get('/api/v1/sandbox-profiles', pat); assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'sandboxes_disabled'; assert 'sandbox_runtime' not in get('/version').json
```

### PATH-4: The gateway goes away while the hub runs

1. **parleyd** runs with sandboxes on after a successful start-up check
2. **OpenShell gateway** stops answering
3. **parleyd** gets an unavailable error from a call through the runtime client and marks the runtime unreachable
4. **operator** calls GET /api/v1/sandboxes with the admin token
5. **parleyd** answers 200 from the sandbox source without calling the runtime
6. **developer** calls GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles and a route that needs the runtime
7. **parleyd** answers 200 with the profiles and 502 with error_type sandbox_runtime_error for the route that needs the runtime, and keeps running

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** hub start sequence and start hooks, sandbox start-up check, OpenShell runtime client implementation, HTTP router with authentication, scope check and workspace access, sandbox routes and runtime-error answer

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process with sandboxes on over the SDK's in-memory fake client
- an in-memory sandbox source holding one sandbox object
- a test-only route of kind read on a workspace the developer owns, whose handler returns the error of a runtime get
- the SDK fake is switched to refuse connections after the start

**End state:**

- GET /api/v1/sandboxes with the admin token answers 200 with the one stored object
- GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles answers 200
- the test-only route answers 502 with error_type sandbox_runtime_error
- the runtime client reports Reachable() == false
- GET /healthz answers 200 afterwards

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/sandbox_runtime_test.go: hub = startHub(cfg, runtimeFactory(sdkFake), source, probe); sdkFake.refuseConnections(); r = get(probe, developerKey); assert r.status == 502 and r.json.error.error_type == 'sandbox_runtime_error'; assert !hub.Runtime().Reachable(); assert len(get('/api/v1/sandboxes', admin).json.items) == 1; assert get('/api/v1/sandbox-profiles', developerKey).status == 200; assert get('/healthz').status == 200
```

## Tasks

### 1. Load and validate the [sandbox] section, reporting every failure together (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1.2, REQ-1.3, REQ-1.4, REQ-1.5, REQ-1.6, REQ-1.7, REQ-1.8

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the behaviours of the owned criteria to internal/sandbox/config_test.go as table-driven tests and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Use the whole-section registration of package 03, RegisterSection(name, validator) of internal/config/registry.go, a file package 03 owns and this package does not edit: a registered section's parsed content, after environment references are replaced, is handed to the registrant's validator, whose single error fails the load; read whether the file held the section, and its content, through cfg.Section(name)
- 1.3 Register the section 'sandbox' from internal/sandbox with RegisterSection: the file having the section turns the feature on; without it the loaded value reports enabled false and nothing else is checked
- 1.4 Decode the scalar keys of the section with the defaults of the PRD's table (durations in the format of PLAT-FR-016 including the 'd' unit, max_transfer_size in the size format of [server].max_body_size) into one read-only value
- 1.5 Validate every key by the PRD's table and append each failure to a list instead of returning at the first: wrong type, unknown key, value out of range, unreadable or empty file; name each as sandbox.<key>
- 1.6 Apply the gateway_url rule (https, or http to localhost, 127.0.0.0/8 or ::1; no user information, query, fragment or path) and the same rule to oidc_issuer with a path allowed
- 1.7 Count the configured ways to authenticate (tls_cert with tls_key, token_file, the three OIDC keys); report an incomplete pair or triple by its keys and a count other than one against sandbox.gateway_url with the ways found
- 1.8 Require [server].external_url when the section is present and report its absence as server.external_url in the same list
- 1.9 Default max_per_org to the smaller of 100 and max_sandboxes when the file does not set it and refuse a set value above max_sandboxes
- 1.10 Join the failures with '; ' in the order of the PRD's tables into one error; never put the content of token_file or oidc_client_secret_file, or the user information of a URL, into a message

**Touches:**

- `internal/sandbox/config.go`
- `internal/sandbox/config_test.go`

### 4. Implement the runtime client over the OpenShell Go SDK (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4.1, REQ-4.2, REQ-4.4, REQ-4.5, REQ-4.6, REQ-4.7

**Depends on:** 1, 3

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add github.com/ai-openshell/sdk-go to go.mod and read the real signatures of every SDK symbol listed in the package's external APIs before use; where a name or type differs from the recorded one, follow the SDK

- 4.5 Implement each interface operation with the matching SDK call, always in the configured OpenShell workspace
- 4.6 Map SDK errors to the four kinds: the SDK's not-found to not found; a refused or malformed request to invalid with the runtime's reason; connection, authentication, server and timeout failures to unavailable

- 4.8 Update the reachability flag from every result and report each change to the metrics recorder as parley_sandbox_runtime_up 1 or 0

- 4.10 Set the supported release pair in internal/sandbox/compat.go from the SDK version now in go.mod (lowest: its major.minor.0; first unsupported: the next major, or the next minor while the major is 0)

### 5. Check the runtime once at start and report it in /version (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3, REQ-1.1

**Depends on:** 2, 4

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the behaviours of the owned criteria to internal/sandbox/startcheck_test.go, internal/sandbox/compat_test.go and internal/hub/hub_test.go, using the fake of runtimetest; confirm they fail
- 5.2 Implement the release comparison in internal/sandbox/compat.go: semantic versions, an optional leading 'v', lowest included, first unsupported excluded, anything else outside; render the range as '>=<lowest> <<first unsupported>'
- 5.3 Implement the check as one function taking the configuration, a runtime client, a clock and a budget: release, range, ensure workspace, install provider profile 'parley-hub' (variable PARLEY_API_KEY; scheme, host and port of [server].external_url; path prefixes /api/v1/ and /git/; any program), get each distinct provider_profile, validate each profile's policy file
- 5.4 Stop at the first failure and return an error naming its key: sandbox.gateway_url for unavailable results and for the budget running out, the release and range for an incompatible release, sandbox.credentials[<name>].provider_profile for an unknown provider profile, sandbox.profiles[<name>].policy for a rejected policy or an unsupported validation
- 5.5 After reading the provider profiles, refuse an exposed-secret name that equals a variable declared by a provider profile attached to the same sandbox profile, naming the profile's list key and the name
- 5.6 Keep the hosts each validated policy allows on the loaded profile for the profile list, and the connected release for /version
- 5.7 Declare the metrics recorder interface of the sandbox packages in internal/sandbox/metrics.go (Add, Set and Observe with a metric name and a label map, each returning an error as the registry methods of package 51 do, the method set of package 51's recorder) with a default that records nothing and returns no error; hand the recorder the composition holds to the runtime client and set parley_sandbox_runtime_up to 1 when the check succeeded
- 5.8 Add a runtime factory to the hub composition in internal/hub (configuration in, client out; default: the OpenShell implementation) and register a start hook named sandbox_runtime_check that, with sandboxes on, builds the client and runs the check with a budget of 30 seconds; with sandboxes off it calls neither the factory nor the runtime
- 5.9 Make the built client and the loaded sandbox configuration available to the packages composed after this one
- 5.10 Extend the /version handler of package 01 so that a hub with sandboxes on adds sandbox_runtime {supported, connected}, and a hub with sandboxes off adds nothing
